A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPRI research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original cognitive-reappraisal evaluations, BiGGen Bench correlations, seed ablations and supervised fine-tuning results, with full results in Appendices F–H.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by token-use and cost estimates in Appendix B and intermediate model outputs and critiques in Appendix J.

M1.justification: The two-stage algorithm, Equations (1)–(6), stopping criteria, prompts and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix J documents previously omitted iterations; the suggestion of cheaper critics does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both retain the 30 Reddit posts, eight-capability BiGGen subset, Dolly and MixInstruct training data, and the same six SFT evaluation benchmarks. Added cost analyses and expanded examples concern existing tasks and inputs.

E2.justification: Corresponding performance and ablation tables retain the same comparator sets. The new cost tables evaluate existing methods; Ramji et al. and AlpacaFarm are added as related work, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Appendix B introduces per-response input/output-token accounting and whole-task cost estimation using API prices, with Dolly specified for SFT costing. Existing splits, sample sizes, generation settings and quality-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B extends the existing model-call analysis with token usage and costs. Appendix J expands retained case studies with critic feedback and rejected intermediate drafts, illustrating principle and response refinement. The seed ablations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain reappraisal pairwise t-tests at p < 0.05 and BiGGen correlation significance reporting at p < 0.001. No repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added; the new costs are point estimates.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and the matched appendix performance tables retain their values. New Tables 5–7 add token/cost results, including Dolly SPRI costs of $13.3 for the base model and $11.5 for the critic. Appendix J adds intermediate outputs and critic scores, rather than revised final benchmark outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the SFT formulation in Section 5.1 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: context-situated principles with minimal oversight, expert-comparable reappraisal, improved instance-specific judging and truthfulness gains from synthetic SFT data.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.4 discusses fewer model calls versus critic overhead, proposes cheaper critics and asserts savings over expert-written guidance and crowdsourced rubrics. These add efficiency interpretations; cheaper-critic performance and human-labor savings are not measured.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly discloses token consumption and estimated costs separately for base and critic models, identifying OpenAI and TogetherAI pricing sources. Existing prompts, generation hyperparameters, LoRA and hardware descriptions, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands its feedback discussion with Ramji et al. (2024) on external-metric refinement and Dubois et al. (2023) on AlpacaFarm, plus fuller explanations of existing references. SPRI's central positioning remains unchanged; publication updates to retained references are not additional works.

P1.justification: The revision adds a cost appendix and generic impact statement, expands related-work prose and example annotations, and corrects typos such as 'Oralce' and 'pertaining'. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Three cost tables are added, Table 2's caption explicitly identifies Pearson correlation, and examples gain iteration labels and pass/fail markers. Figures 1–3 and the existing result-table designs remain, with local reflow and appendix renumbering.

improvement.justification: Appendix B makes computational requirements assessable, and Appendix J exposes critique/refinement traces omitted from v1, providing useful transparency without changing the benchmark evidence. The gain is limited by the cost interpretation: despite B.4 describing comparable total SFT costs, Table 7 lists $24.8 for SPRI including its critic, versus $12.2 for self-instruct and $13.4 for self-align. Proposed cheaper-critic and human-labor savings remain unvalidated.
